description: Apply a batch of adds, updates and deletes to a site's user redirect rules, in order, as one change: all of them or none. Use this, or `set_redirects`, for bulk work rather than many single calls. Rule ids come from `list_redirects` and start with `r_`. File rules can't be changed here: an operation naming a file rule's line answers `FileRule`, with the `line` and the operation's `index`. Pass the `version` from `list_redirects` to refuse the batch if the rules changed since (`StaleVersion`, with the latest version). One invalid rule refuses the batch with `InvalidRules`, listing each error by the operation's `index`. Redirects apply only on the organization's own custom domains (`CustomDomainRequired` otherwise). Visitors get the change within about 5 minutes.

operations.description: Applied in order, each to the list the ones before it left.

position.description: Where to add the rule among the user rules, from 0. Defaults to the end.

from.description: Source path: exact (`/old-page`), with `:name` placeholders (`/blog/:year/:slug`), or ending in `/*` (`/docs/*`). No query string.

status.description: 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308. Defaults to 301, a permanent move. Use 302 or 307 for a temporary one.

to.description: Destination: a path starting with `/`, or an http(s) URL. `:splat` fills in what `*` matched, and `:name` a placeholder's value. The request's query string is carried over.

partition.description: Data partition the site lives in. Omit to use the user's home partition.

version.description: The `version` the rules were read at, from `list_redirects`. Omit to apply the batch to whatever the latest list is.

name: edit_redirects
